precepts.text: The children of Israel pitch their tents every man by his own camp and his own standard: Judah with Judah, Ephraim with Ephraim.
precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Just before this, the Lord says, “I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds”, and that healing came when he sent Christ to die on the cross: by his stripes we are healed. “because they called thee an Outcast”: outcast means African-American, made-up names for our race, a Zion “whom no man seeketh after”. Nobody gives a damn about blacks and Latinos. Then: “Behold, I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents”.

What are Jacob’s tents? “And the children of Israel shall pitch their tents, every man by his own camp, and every man by his own standard, throughout their hosts.” Every man by his own camp: Judah is going to be with Judah, Ephraim with Ephraim, Benjamin with Benjamin. That is the restructuring, the restoration of a nation.

And every man by his own standard: Judah had the standard of the lion, Benjamin the wolf, Naphtali the deer, Ephraim the bull. When the Lord brings again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, all of this is being restored again: the tribes set back in order, each under its own standard.

precepts.text: The officers released the man with a new house, a new vineyard, a new wife, and the fearful man, lest his brethren's heart faint as well as his heart.
precepts.point: The Most High chose able men. In the book of Judges He cut the army down from the thousands to three hundred; and when Moses held up his hands over the battle, mighty men had to hold his arms up.

note.label: Numbers 1: The Numbering of the Armies of Israel

precepts.why:
The book of Numbers is the numbering of the armies of the Lord, the armies of the children of Israel: every male “From twenty years old and upward, all that are able to go forth to war in Israel.” Every man went to war unless the law released him, and this is the law that released him.

The officers spoke to the people before the battle. “What man is there that hath built a new house, and hath not dedicated it? let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man dedicate it.” The same for the man that “hath planted a vineyard, and hath not yet eaten of it”, and for the man that “hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her”: let him go and return unto his house. A man that had newly married, or built a house and not dedicated it, did not have to go.

Then the officers spoke further: “What man is there that is fearful and fainthearted? let him go and return unto his house, lest his brethren’s heart faint as well as his heart.” The fearful man did not have to go either, because that spirit of fear would jump on the other brothers. The armies numbered in Numbers 1 were the able men, and the Most High chose able men.

precepts.text: By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you; the Most High cut the army down to able men of His choosing.
precepts.point: The Most High chose able men. In the book of Judges He cut the army down from the thousands to three hundred; and when Moses held up his hands over the battle, mighty men had to hold his arms up.

note.label: Numbers 1: The Numbering of the Armies of Israel

precepts.why:
Moses and Aaron numbered every man able to go forth to war by their armies, but the Most High chose able men, and He was never bound to the numbers. In the book of Judges He cut the army down from the thousands to three hundred.

“And the Lord said unto Gideon, By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you, and deliver the Midianites into thine hand: and let all the other people go every man unto his place.” He sent the rest home and saved Israel by the three hundred of His choosing.

So the numbering of the armies in Numbers 1 is the numbering of the men the Lord could use, and the Lord chose which able men would win His battles.

precepts.text: When Moses held up his hand Israel prevailed, and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands until the going down of the sun.
precepts.point: The Most High chose able men. In the book of Judges He cut the army down from the thousands to three hundred; and when Moses held up his hands over the battle, mighty men had to hold his arms up.

note.label: Numbers 1: The Numbering of the Armies of Israel

precepts.why:
The armies numbered here were the men able to go forth to war, and the Most High chose able men. When Moses held up his hands over the battle, mighty men had to hold his arms up.

“And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.” When his hands grew heavy “they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.”

That is the kind of able men the Lord numbered by their armies: men who could stand with the man of God the whole day until the battle was won.

precepts.text: Promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south; God is the judge: he putteth down one, and setteth up another.
precepts.point: The Most High always chose the men He wanted. It is not up to us to choose who is going to be leadership or who will be in this or that position; it is never us. Promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south: God is the judge, He putteth down one and setteth up another, and He elected these men as renowned men.

note.label: Numbers 1: The Numbering of the Armies of Israel

precepts.why:
With Moses and Aaron stood a man of every tribe, each one head of the house of his fathers: “These were the renowned of the congregation, princes of the tribes of their fathers, heads of thousands in Israel.” The Most High named them Himself; He always chose the men He wanted.

“For promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south. But God is the judge: he putteth down one, and setteth up another.” It is not up to us to choose who is going to be leadership or who will be in this or that position; it is never us. God is the judge, and He elected these men as renowned men.

So the list of princes in Numbers 1 is not a list Israel voted on. Elizur, Shelumiel, Nahshon and the rest were set up by the One who putteth down one and setteth up another.

precepts.text: The congregation declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers.
precepts.point: Pedigrees are declared by the house of the fathers, so the line is reckoned through the father even here.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

precepts.why:
“And they assembled all the congregation together on the first day of the second month, and they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers”. Pedigrees are declared by the house of the fathers.

“Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters.” He gave his daughter “to Jarha his servant to wife”, an Egyptian, “and she bare him Attai.” The line is carried down from their child, and even here it is reckoned through the father: Attai begat Nathan, Nathan begat Zabad, and on down to Elishama.
